more_info.overview: Aspartame-acesulfame salt is used as a sweetener in food. Its technological role is to provide sweetness.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include meal replacement for weight control as referred to in Commission Regulation (EU) no 432/2012, flavoured drinks, flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products, edible ices. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Made by combining aspartame and acesulfame potassium in acidic solution and crystallising the resulting salt. Potassium and moisture are removed during processing.
more_info.daily_intake: Component limits: 40 mg aspartame/kg body weight/day and 15 mg acesulfame K/kg body weight/day (EFSA, 2026). No separate salt ADI was derived.
more_info.side_effects:
The salt separates into its two sweetener components. Their assessed food-use exposure raised no concern in 2026.
The assessment applies the separate component intake limits.
